correctness.summary: For three colours on paths and cycles, successful partial assignments are exactly restrictions of proper 3-colourings obtained by deleting independent sets of eligible degree-two vertices. A sign encoding gives the path recurrence, while a four-state transfer matrix and root-of-unity filter give the cycle recurrences. Multiplicativity and elementary degree constraints complete the all-lambda classification. Exhaustive definition-level verification through path and cycle order 8 matched all recurrences and specializations.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The primary 2026 paper and the earlier Farr-Morgan preprint were inspected, and searches using forced-colouring, forced-coloring, path, cycle, and maximum-degree-two terminology found no family recurrences or maximum-degree-two classification. The earlier paper already contains the corrected P3 value, so that correction is not claimed as original. The 2025 Springer chapter corresponding to the preprint was identified but not separately checked line-by-line; additions unique to its final text and unindexed recent work are the principal residual risks.

value.summary: The result completely evaluates a natural boundary class for a graph polynomial whose fixed-parameter evaluation is generally #P-hard for every lambda at least three. It supplies short recurrences, linear-time evaluation on maximum-degree-two graphs, exact minimum forcing-domain sizes, and two consistency corrections to the current v1 formulas.

limitations: The theorem does not address maximum degree at least three.
The final 2025 Springer chapter was not separately checked line-by-line beyond its open preprint counterpart.
The recency of the invariant leaves residual risk from unindexed parallel work.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
